title: Bir Tawil: Nobody's Land
status: approved by the user 2026-10-31 ("Approve all three"), no edits

lines.text: From this desert, you're standing on land no country claims.
Egypt to the north. Sudan to the south.
Two thousand and sixty square kilometres, and neither country will take it.
Zoom out, and there are two borders.
In 1899, it was a straight line: the twenty-second parallel.
In 1902, Britain drew a second one, around who actually used the land.
Each country picks the line that gives it Halaib. Ten times bigger, and on the sea.
No towns. No coast. Just herders and gold miners passing through.
In 2000, Sudan pulled its forces out of Halaib.
Egypt has run it ever since.
Two lines. Two countries. And one desert with zero owners.

respellNotes.Halaib: misaki default hˈælAb ('HAL-abe') -> hˌɑlɑjˈib ('Hah-lah-yeeb'; whisper hears 'Hala'ib' / 'Halaib'; hˌɑlɑˈib was heard as 'Halloween')
